family_assessments.assessment: The intended challenge is to recover one effective trustee handover at a bank-meeting cut-off, despite signed papers and a later administrative message. The blind review found that an affirmative hold preserves the incumbent and a registered release effects simultaneous retirement and replacement (family_a/review/blind-review.md). Fresh excerpt checks verified the joint instrument-and-disposition routes and rejected a proposed shorter route (family_a/review/necessity.md). The order-only sibling held the Source bytes, key and ordinary context fixed (family_a/review/matched-sources.json). Bank and administrative records add an ordinary supported kinship and plausible non-operative cues. Recency and name frequency favour the incumbent, while promotion of draft material favours the successor; the small, expressly framed office limits generalisation. Retain for the release-versus-positive-hold contrast and the separate order control.
family_assessments.overlap: Joint proof recurs in B and C. D keeps effectiveness fixed and varies scope. A does not test whether silence about release can establish non-release.

family_assessments.assessment: The intended challenge is to attribute a native parentage report using an independently maintained attendance field. Completing the field binds the statement to one named speaker (family_b/review/outputs/comparison.json); two compatible speakers remain with the incomplete field, and the ordinary parent edge survives both conditions (family_b/review/agreement.json). The forward and export share an informant, and forward-only readings did not fix the speaker (family_b/review/mask-results.json). Deleting a necessary identity or statement fact defeats only the dependent target (family_b/review/proof-deletions.json). An original-document sighting supplies incidental ordinary kinship. Testing field completeness and taking the first contact can reproduce the edge delta; the fictional desk convention and two candidates bound the result. Retain for attribution and provenance, not for general identity ambiguity.
family_assessments.overlap: C withholds when a reference cannot identify a trust, whereas B cannot identify the speaker. F keeps identities complete. B traces copies of one origin; it does not reconcile independent contradictory witnesses.

family_assessments.assessment: The intended challenge is to identify which trust an operative designation concerns. Swapping the linked parent-deed reference switches the licensed endpoint; obscuring the distinguishing character leaves both allocations viable (family_c/review/outputs/comparison.json), and both readers withheld both endpoints in that condition (family_c/review/agreement.json). Independent excerpt readers verified the three-Source proof, and whole-file masks defeated the target while preserving ten ordinary edges (family_c/review/proof-deletions.json). Shared trustees, routine meeting and expense material, and a wish letter add context without an independent distraction intervention. First-trust, fixed-trust and assign-both rules fail across variants, but one register entry and two parallel settlements bound the join. Retain for distributed proof and the invariant-graph check.
family_assessments.overlap: A and B also require dependent evidence. C joins a designation to a trust, not a report to its speaker or an instrument to its operative release. Its completeness check does not identify a placement or workload effect.

family_assessments.assessment: The approved scoped-amendment hypothesis predicted that changing only the provision locator would switch the earlier survivor while preserving the replacement, named trust and unaffected relationships. The D0/D1 comparison in the coverage register reports that exact result, and the closing audit independently verified the grouped scope proof attached to each current beneficiary. The separate office provisions and fixed effective date add context but are not independently varied. Individual fact-level deletions remain incomplete, and reading the locator alone can reproduce the graph without recovering the joint proof. The demonstrated invariants are trust relationships; unrelated kinship was not tested. Retain the express scope comparison without claiming exhaustive fact necessity or coverage of other amendment mechanisms.
family_assessments.overlap: A varies whether an act takes effect; D fixes effect and varies its reach. C resolves a trust endpoint; D keeps the trust fixed and resolves which existing provision the amendment displaces.

family_assessments.assessment: The approved complete-record label-collision hypothesis predicted invariance of both the exact named graph and the valid proof routes under one populated display-label edit. The F0/F1 comparison reports that both graphs and their separately attached proof sets stayed fixed; the masked review found that withholding an exact identity entry defeated its dependent edge. The original isolated excerpt reader explained the correct identity but entered a different structured surname; the independent identical-packet repeat returned the correct surname. That discrepancy limits any claim of uniform exact-name recovery. The working index is genuinely ancillary in the comparison, but positional pairing remains available. Retain for this bounded collision and distinguish correct graph recovery from correct attached identity proof.
family_assessments.overlap: B withholds because attribution is incomplete; F retains complete distinguishing evidence and varies only a display label. F does not establish robustness to collisions in authoritative identifiers or to interacting gaps.

gaps.finding: B verifies common origin, not how independent accounts should be reconciled. E reproduced a concordance-to-withholding contrast but returned on retainer relevance and witness-reference provenance; E0/E1 are diagnostic only. W is a retained attempt, not admitted evidence. Independent issuance also does not by itself establish independent knowledge of every field.

B and C show local withholding and A shows an affirmative hold. They do not establish when bounded records positively support non-occurrence within an exhaustive set of permitted routes. T technically qualifies an affirmative inspection-scope proof, not that negative-coverage inference. Do not label a joint proof or a review mask a measured interaction.

A and D isolate release and express amendment reach. The packet does not establish coverage of fixed versus rolling incorporation of independently issued records, or field-specific attestation over an unchanged mixed-origin payload. D's grouped proof is verified; complete individual fact-level deletion coverage remains open.

B and F give complementary, bounded attribution and display-label tests. Broader authoritative identifier collisions and interacting gaps remain open. F's positional shortcut and B's first-contact shortcut limit claims about the reasoning behind a correct graph.

C verifies invariant completeness and A provides one byte-fixed order control. X technically qualifies a relationship-support edit in native correspondence, not a burial or placement effect. T's intermediate natural file does not identify a volume effect or discharge the separate large-tier commitment. Document count and length describe workload.

Retrieval, requesting missing records, OCR and physical text recovery require a different study. A supplied record can describe a missing artifact or field; score only the resulting support for relationships. Practitioner outcomes and prevalence likewise remain outside scope.

result.portfolio_summary: The register contains five admitted Matter histories: A, B, C, D and F. Count each once, including its matched conditions. Joint proof and evidence sufficiency recur across the portfolio; named-endpoint resolution recurs in B, C and F; documentary authority recurs in A and D, but effectiveness and amendment reach are distinct controls. A isolates presentation order. C checks recovery of a substantial invariant graph, not the effect of administrative load. These are independent review findings about support and proof, not paid extraction observations. Outside the admitted set, X technically qualifies a matched incidental assertion in native correspondence, T technically qualifies a supplied-record inspection-scope case at intermediate workload, and N revision 3 is technically qualified for executed-counterpart coverage. X and T await human admission; none of the three adds to the admitted count. E remains diagnostic only after return at the documentary-realism gate. Retained roadmap attempts are not credited as demonstrated coverage. AB and AD were selected in the first reserve round; neither is duplicated here. AA and AC remain held. Rank this second reserve AG, AH, AJ: AG tests whether the scope of independently issued records establishes a condition by excluding every permitted alternative; AH isolates which fields an issuer actually vouches for in a mixed-origin report, at lower review cost; AJ tests an express choice between fixed and rolling incorporation, with the greatest documentary-realism risk. Ten families is a planning target, not a quota, and the 19-history pre-giant technical goal is a separate milestone. Intermediate and large workload tiers remain separate commitments. No proposal counts as qualified or admitted.

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers check exact excerpts for the named default and exhaustive rule, the coverage and nil result of each independent route, and the temporal comparison. Verify the complete same-edge subset and reject each singleton and plausible short route; identify the exact uncovered interval in the partial branch.

Remove each report separately; separately delete the exhaustive-route rule, one needed coverage bound, and a nil finding, including copies of each deleted fact. Independently rederive each diagnostic graph. Audit for a summary, later extract or alternate receipt trail that would settle the target without the planned route.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: Only support for the named default edge changes. The shorter extract leaves a qualifying receipt possible in the uncovered interval; it neither establishes such a receipt nor disproves the default. No alternative beneficiary or negative predicate is emitted.
genres_and_provenance: Verified governing extract from the trustees' executed file: establishes the default, the permitted routes and window, and an unrelated current office.
Native nomination circular retained by the trustee secretary and issued before the window: explains the opportunity and submission arrangements to recipients, without certifying receipt or outcome.
Electronic intake activity extract issued by the portal operator from its maintained receipt log and retained with the trustees' reconciliation records: accounts for one channel over a stated period.

Paper intake activity extract issued by the separately responsible receiving office from its own inbound records and retained for the same reconciliation: accounts for the other channel over its stated period.
Dated adviser brief retained for the post-window review: fixes the evidence cut-off and purpose without declaring the outcome.
design.intervention: Change exactly one literal period-end field in the paper intake extract, from coverage through the end of the nomination window to coverage ending within it. Fix all other bytes, including issue time, nil result, window and Source order.
invariants: The trust, named default, qualifying receipt rule, report authors and bases, printed nil results, issue and receipt chronology, and cut-off remain fixed.
The independently supported office and its proof stay fixed.
negative_controls: The nomination circular documents an opportunity, not a nomination or its receipt.
The unrelated office survives both branches and the target-only diagnostics.
design.scenario: The adviser receives separate ordinary activity reports for the authorised receipt routes. One always covers the full window. The other either covers the full window or stops short, without purporting to say what happened afterward.
shortcut_heuristics: Test nil-means-none, missing-means-none, one-channel suffices, and issue-date-as-coverage rules. Headings and filenames must not mark an extract as case-closing. A period-end token may predict the delta but is not sufficient proof.
success_criteria: Two isolated whole-file readers per branch independently reconstruct the complete exact-name graph; fresh readers verify the positive subset, the partial branch's precise evidentiary gap and each removal result.
Stop if either extract is merely a search result, the partial export is unnatural, authorised off-log receipt is possible, or an ordinarily available definitive close-out would have to be suppressed.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and integration 9–14; blind whole-file and fresh excerpt and removal review 10–15; adjudication and audit 7–11; owner review 2–4. Assumes two readers per branch and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 5 natural Sources. The operative extract and circular serve different purposes; each intake operator accounts for its own channel, and the brief sets the review boundary.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse exact-byte comparison, A's cut-off checks, independently rederived diagnostic keys and same-edge proof assessment.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Score beneficiary_of and the invariant trust office only. Negative receipt findings, coverage and unresolved alternatives belong in the companion register.
risks_and_limits: This tests bounded coverage under one express default rule, not general proof of absence, a two-factor effect or the reliability of real receipt systems.

assumptions: The fictional instrument expressly states the exhaustive receipt routes, the qualifying act, boundary conventions and automatic consequence. No further approval is required. The two extracts establish completeness only for their respective routes and stated periods, with no unaddressed logging lag, manual bypass or exception.

Both period ends are credible for the same ordinary reconciliation export and precede its fixed issue time. The two reports reach the adviser after the window closes and before the briefing. The partial-period export can naturally be received without an already available closing certificate or live log in the advice pack.
grounding.documentary_situation: The supplied terms give a named default effect if no qualifying nomination was received through either of two expressly permitted routes during the window. The two independently maintained receipt systems each issue a bounded activity extract for reconciliation. Both show no relevant receipts within their stated periods; one period may leave part of the window unaccounted for.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile the receipt records for a time-limited nomination window before the trustees use the current beneficiary provision for planning.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Identify the supported beneficiary relationship and distinguish a verified absence of a qualifying receipt from incomplete records of the window.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether this trust would naturally permit two separately operated receipt routes and retain bounded activity extracts with explicit completeness statements.
Whether the two reports would ordinarily reach the adviser at the same review stage without a controlling closure summary.

references.relevance: Grounds retention of instruments and supporting decision records, not a nomination procedure, the completeness of a receipt system or the effect of a default clause.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Trust administration advice on whether the supplied file establishes the named default provision after the nomination window closed.

objective.coverage_gap: A uses a positive hold to defeat release; it cannot diagnose an affirmative default inferred from exhaustive negative coverage. T verifies which items an affirmative inspection covered, not whether independent records jointly exclude all permitted triggering events. R moves an observed event across a deadline; AG holds the recorded nil results fixed and changes what they can exclude.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may equate a nil result with absence throughout the window, or refuse to credit a documented negative even when all permitted routes are covered. It may recover the correct default edge but cite only the instrument or one receipt record.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: With the same nil entries and the window closed in both conditions, the named default edge is supported only when the records jointly cover every permitted receipt route throughout the window. Full graph recovery and sufficient attachment in both branches disconfirm the predicted errors.

proposals.title: A default provision requires complete negative receipt coverage

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers examine the exact printed values, respondent attribution, affirmative comparison and its scope together, then test the strongest singleton Sources and partial excerpts. Verify that the identical checked identifiers do not license parentage in the narrow branch.

Separately delete the focal value, the affirmative finding and the necessary scope fact with their copies, and independently rederive each diagnostic graph. Mask the request to see whether its text is actually needed or merely explains the work. Audit both directions for an independently sufficient assertion and for any source of the working value that would turn it into evidence.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The focal parent_of edge is supported only when the signed affirmative comparison reaches the printed parent field. Identifiers-only scope leaves that field unverified, not denied. Credit an exact sufficient subset from the response alone if the response supplies all required facts.
genres_and_provenance: Client's signed current drafting instructions retained by the advising practice: supply the planning task and an unrelated firsthand family relationship, without settling the focal claim.
Holder's signed authority retained by the checking practice and supplied to the adviser: permits inspection and scoped reporting rather than unrestricted copying of the record.
Adviser's native check request retained on both files: supplies provisional particulars and asks for a report of which checks have actually been completed, without asserting parentage.
Checking practice's signed response retained as issued and received: reproduces the pending values for reconciliation and states the affirmative scope of the direct comparison.
Dated adviser review brief retained on the planning file: sets the cut-off and decisions needed before drafting without summarising the check result.
design.intervention: Replace exactly one literal scope span in the signed comparison statement, narrowing the affirmative result from subject identifiers and parentage to subject identifiers only. Hold every other byte and Source order fixed, including the printed values, sighted record and attribution.
invariants: Exact names, issuer, record sighted, request, issue and receipt dates, cut-off and the verified subject identifiers remain the same.
The unrelated relationship and its sufficient proof are fixed.
negative_controls: The copied working entry and inspection authority do not establish parentage. The independent firsthand relationship survives both conditions and focal diagnostics.
design.scenario: The same working values appear on both issued responses. One certifies their agreement with the sighted record only for subject identifiers; the other also certifies agreement for the recorded parent. This is verification of a record entry, not adjudication of legal parentage.
shortcut_heuristics: Test signed-means-verified, copied-means-unusable and relationship-keyword rules. Check headings and filenames for an answer and confirm that the signature covers exactly the stated comparison, not every printed field.
success_criteria: Two isolated readers per branch reconstruct the complete exact-name graph; fresh readers verify sufficient attachment, the continuing identity check and the exact reason for withholding.
Stop if field-limited checking would not naturally leave the proposed value visible, if broader coverage requires changing another record, or if the request or holder independently settles parentage.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring 7–11; blind and fresh excerpt and removal review 8–12; adjudication and audit 5–8; owner review 2–3. Assumes two readers per branch and one pre-lock wording revision at most.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 5 natural Sources. The instructions, permission, request, issued check and advice brief serve distinct purposes before the cut-off.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse B's origin tracing, matched-byte checks, exact singleton review and same-edge sufficiency assessment.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use parent_of and any independently supported invariant kinship. Authority to inspect, identity verification and open comparisons remain in the companion register.
risks_and_limits: The scoped phrase may be lexically easy. This tests endorsement of a particular field, not difficulty, the reliability of civil records or how practitioners resolve disputed parentage.

assumptions: The requester has a genuine need to tell completed checks from pending checks. The printed proposed parent value is an explicitly unverified working entry, not an attributed firsthand account. Only the response's signed scope and affirmative comparison can establish agreement with the full record.

An interim identifiers-only result and a results return including the parentage comparison are both natural before the same advice meeting. The response must be self-contained about the values and checked fields; no unseen certificate is needed to interpret it.
grounding.documentary_situation: A checking practice returns an issued response that carries forward the requesting adviser's provisional entries beside a signed comparison statement. The checker sighted the same full record in both conditions. The signed scope covers the subject identifiers in both, but covers the populated parentage field in only one.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile contact particulars and requested civil-record checks before updating private-client drafting instructions.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Distinguish particulars checked against the civil record from retained working values that have not been verified.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether a checking practice would return populated provisional values with an explicit affirmative scope statement, rather than blank unchecked fields or issue a fully transcribed sighting.
Whether the instruction, holder authority and partial result would naturally co-exist by the advice cut-off without a more definitive record.

references.relevance: Grounds the availability of parentage entries in a full civil record, not the scope of any professional attestation.
references.title: GRO · How to order civil registration records

references.relevance: Grounds retaining instructions and updates in a drafting matter, not the proposed division of the checking work.
references.title: SRA · Drafting and preparation of wills

grounding.retainer: Planning advice following transfer of earlier papers, including a limited check of particulars used to identify a person mentioned in the drafting file.

objective.coverage_gap: I varies the underlying record basis of a certified transcription. AH holds the underlying record and printed payload fixed and varies which propositions the issuer adopts as independently checked within one issued document. T joins a named worksheet item to the contents of an inspected folder; AH holds the item and its inspection fixed and distinguishes what was checked about it. L changes available content; AH leaves the focal field populated in both branches.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may treat an independent signature as independent verification of every value printed on the document, or reject the entire response as derivative even when the signed result expressly verifies the relevant field.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: Holding the printed values, the sighted record and issue status fixed, changing only the stated coverage of the affirmative comparison changes support for one named parent edge. Correct recovery and precise proof attachment in both branches disconfirm blanket endorsement and blanket rejection on this file.

proposals.title: A signed check vouches only for the fields it covers

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers verify exact passages for the trust and authority, the incorporation mode and the linked issue, chronology and named row. Check singletons and shorter routes, including whether either issue or an accounts document independently states the current provision.

Delete the mode, series linkage and selected row separately, removing any copies of each fact. Mask each schedule issue separately and independently rederive both keys rather than assuming fallback to the remaining issue. Record exact support for excluding the inapplicable issue without scoring a negative.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The fixed branch supports only the earlier row under the focal provision; the rolling branch supports only the updated row. Both use sufficient same-edge proof of the applicable version. A payment or the inapplicability of a row does not supply a separate scored predicate.
genres_and_provenance: Verified principal extract retained by the trustees: names the trust, supplies express incorporation authority and establishes an unaffected trust relationship.
Executed adoption decision retained in the trustees' decision file: identifies the schedule series and defines how its issues apply, with effect before the later issue.
Earlier signed schedule issued and archived by the separately authorised schedule keeper: records the row in force in that series at adoption.
Later signed schedule issued and retained by the same keeper as its updated record: changes the row before the advice cut-off without itself declaring what the trust adopted.
Earlier-period payment reconciliation retained by the trust accountant: explains historical payments without proving who is currently named.
Dated adviser brief retained on the review file: fixes the cut-off and the prospective decision without repeating either roster.
design.intervention: Change exactly one literal incorporation-rule span in the adoption decision, choosing between the issue current at adoption and the properly updated series. Do not change the series identifier, execution, dates, schedule content, other Source bytes or order.
invariants: Adoption date and effectiveness, both schedule issues and their sequence, named persons, cut-off and scope of the affected provision stay fixed.
The unrelated trust relationship and historical payment evidence stay fixed.
negative_controls: The old reconciliation is compatible with either current result; masking it leaves both keys unchanged. An unaffected trust relationship survives target-only diagnostics.
design.scenario: The schedule issuer records a new version in its normal cycle. The advisers must distinguish succession within the issuer's records from a change to the particular provision that refers to those records.
shortcut_heuristics: Test newest-only, freeze-at-signature, union and file-position rules. Natural revision labels may identify sequence but must not announce which issue governs the trust.
success_criteria: Two isolated whole-file readers per branch recover the complete graphs and identify which rule selects the row; fresh excerpt and removal readers verify the sufficient subsets and invariant proofs.

Stop if either incorporation mode requires outside law, lacks an ordinary business purpose, would change the reason the later schedule was issued, or would require suppressing a contemporaneous controlling decision.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and chronology integration 10–16; blind and fresh excerpt and removal review 10–15; adjudication and audit 7–11; owner review 3–5. Assumes two readers per branch and a documentary review before drafting.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 6 natural Sources. Two independently issued schedules have distinct version histories and audit purposes; the principal extract, decision, historical reconciliation and brief each do different work.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse D's scope checks, A's chronology checks, exact-byte verification, independently rederived mask keys and same-edge proof assessment.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use beneficiary_of and existing invariant trust predicates. Version status, incorporation, authority and payment are evidence or companion-register context, not nodes or predicates.
risks_and_limits: Defer at the realism gate if the two modes and common retention chronology cannot be justified. A contrived decision written only to make the mode edit work adds no useful coverage.

assumptions: The fictional governing extract expressly permits both modes and states the authority and conditions for issuing schedule updates. The decision is effective in both conditions. Schedule issue by itself neither amends the trust nor makes the old issue inoperative for a provision that adopted it as a fixed snapshot.

The schedule series serves a continuing records function independent of the one decision, so both issues would be created in both branches. The earlier payment period ends before the later issue and is consistent with both branches.
grounding.documentary_situation: An effective trustee decision references a separately issued schedule series. One signed issue was current when the decision took effect. A later properly issued update changes one named row before the review. Both issues are retained for audit; only the incorporation rule determines which row governs the provision under review.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile a retained trustee decision with the schedule series used for a periodic trust review.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Determine whether the decision incorporates the schedule as adopted or incorporates properly issued updates, separately from reconciling earlier payments.
practitioner_unknowns: Whether the same schedule series could naturally serve both modes and be independently maintained without a later trustee decision that would itself resolve the current provision.
Whether both issued schedules would be supplied together for this review without a definitive current roster that bypasses the comparison.

references.relevance: Grounds retention of decisions, supporting schedules and payment records. It does not establish authority to incorporate a schedule or the effect of later issues.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Advise on the current named provision before the trustees instruct the next distribution workstream.

objective.coverage_gap: S varies operative versus administrative use of a fixed list; AJ makes the reference operative in both branches and varies whether subsequent issues flow through it. Q applies a later consolidation rule to an earlier reconstructed subset; AJ has no later trustee consolidation or new adopting act. C switches an identifying reference, whereas AJ keeps the series reference unchanged.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may prefer the latest issue even when the reference is fixed, freeze any reference at signature, or union both issues. It may select the right name without showing why that issue governs.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: Changing only the temporal semantics of the same effective reference switches the supported named edge after an independently issued update. Correct exclusive recovery in both branches with the governing authority, selection rule and applicable row attached disconfirms those shortcuts.

proposals.title: A later issue matters only under rolling incorporation

stopping_criteria: Before authoring, require a credible participant, business purpose, issue time, retention path and availability by the cut-off for every Source in each branch. Drop or defer a design that needs padding, a bespoke support document, an ordinarily available controlling record to be suppressed, or a rule not stated in the fictional file.

Before locking, require two isolated complete-file reconstructions per condition, exact graph-to-file and file-to-graph audit, fresh checks of sufficient subsets and withholding grounds, and independent rederivation after removing necessary components and their copies. If a matched edit changes an unrelated fact or needed proof, or the central claim has an unintended shorter route, revise once or stop.

Keep qualification, human admission and research claims separate. Preserve existing admitted hypotheses, keys and scores. Do not add predicates, score denials, require all alternative valid proofs, or turn review masks into scored conditions.

Stop expanding when a candidate duplicates a stronger retained test, the distinctive mechanism cannot be defended against the identified shortcut, or full-context delivery and independent review cannot be sustained at the proposed load. Do not fill a target by padding dossiers or substituting section keys for whole-file reconstruction.
